page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 16 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY CPU clocked at 2.5 GHz. Constructed on x86_64 architecture, the processor consists of 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system provides 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB memory allocation per vCPU. No local SSD storage is attached to this instance, requiring external block storage options. Network performance is provisioned with a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and the host contains no dedicated GPU hardware. Hardware capabilities include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction extensions.

Performance benchmark testing indicates stable multi-core processing alongside lower single-core execution speed. Multi-threaded evaluations in stress-ng and Geekbench yield average scores, while single-threaded tasks like gzip compression perform in lower percentile bands. Uncached memory throughput reaches 76.43 GB/sec for read operations and 55.34 GB/sec for write operations across large block sizes. Workload tests reflect average execution rates for Redis SET commands at 11.3 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 7.83 GB/sec.

The 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers operational cost efficiency for software requiring higher memory allocations without demanding top-tier single-threaded CPU speed. The primary tradeoff lies in moderate single-core benchmark performance, making sequential tasks slower compared to compute-optimized instance types. The ecs.se1.4xlarge server is best suited for in-memory key-value stores, relational database management systems, caching layers, and enterprise backend processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance equipped with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores and 128.0 GB of RAM. Operating on x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading enabled, it delivers an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive workloads. The server lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware features include AVX-512 instruction extensions and hardware AES support. Performance testing reveals average multi-core execution capabilities, including solid Redis throughput of 11.3 million operations per second and stable web serving capabilities, balanced by lower single-core performance metrics. Given its high RAM density relative to CPU core counts, ecs.se1.4xlarge provides operational efficiency for memory-heavy applications, including caching tiers, relational and in-memory databases, enterprise backends, and batch data processing workloads.
